verses.text: The LORD's word came to Jehu son of Hanani with a message against Baasha. The LORD said,
"I lifted you up out of the dust and made you ruler over my people Israel. But you followed the ways of Jeroboam and made my people Israel sin, and their sins have made me angry.
So I am going to wipe out Baasha and his family completely. I will make your family like the family of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Dogs will eat Baasha's family members who die in the city, and birds will eat those who die in the open country."
The rest of what Baasha did, his deeds and his power, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah. His son Elah became king after him.

The LORD's word had come through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha and his family. It was because of all the evil Baasha did in the LORD's eyes, making him angry by what he did, becoming like Jeroboam's family, and also because he killed Jeroboam's family.
In the twenty-sixth year that Asa was king of Judah, Baasha's son Elah became king of Israel in Tirzah. He ruled for two years.

Zimri, one of his officials, who commanded half of his chariots, made a plot against him. Elah was in Tirzah at the time, getting drunk in the house of Arza, the man in charge of the palace in Tirzah.
Zimri came in, struck Elah down, and killed him. This was in the twenty-seventh year that Asa was king of Judah. Then Zimri became king in his place.
As soon as Zimri became king and sat on the throne, he killed Baasha's whole family. He did not leave a single male alive, not among his relatives or his friends.
So Zimri destroyed Baasha's whole family, just as the LORD had said against Baasha through the prophet Jehu.
This happened because of all the sins of Baasha and his son Elah. They sinned and made Israel sin, and they made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry with their worthless idols.
The rest of what Elah did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
In the twenty-seventh year that Asa was king of Judah, Zimri ruled in Tirzah for seven days. The army was camped near Gibbethon, a Philistine town.
The soldiers in the camp heard that Zimri had made a plot and killed the king. So that same day, there in the camp, all Israel made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel.
Then Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and surrounded Tirzah.
When Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the strongest part of the king's palace. He set the palace on fire around himself and died.
He died because of the sins he committed. He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, following the ways of Jeroboam and the sin Jeroboam had made Israel commit.
The rest of what Zimri did, and his plot against the king, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Then the people of Israel split into two groups. Half of them wanted to make Tibni son of Ginath king, and the other half followed Omri.
But Omri's followers were stronger than the followers of Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died, and Omri became king.
In the thirty-first year that Asa was king of Judah, Omri became king of Israel. He ruled for twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for about seventy kilograms of silver. He built a city on the hill and named it Samaria, after Shemer, who had owned the hill.
Omri did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He was more wicked than all the kings before him.
He followed all the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat and the sins Jeroboam had made Israel commit. They made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry with their worthless idols.
The rest of what Omri did, and the power he showed, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Omri died and was buried in Samaria. His son Ahab became king after him.
In the thirty-eighth year that Asa was king of Judah, Omri's son Ahab became king of Israel. Ahab son of Omri ruled over Israel in Samaria for twenty-two years.
Ahab son of Omri did more evil in the LORD's eyes than all the kings before him.
As if it were not enough to commit the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he also married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians. Then he began to serve Baal and worship him.
He set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he built in Samaria.
Ahab also made an Asherah pole. He did more to make the LORD, the God of Israel, angry than all the kings of Israel before him.

While Ahab was king, Hiel from Bethel rebuilt Jericho. Laying its foundations cost him the life of his oldest son Abiram, and setting up its gates cost him the life of his youngest son Segub. This happened just as the LORD had said through Joshua son of Nun.
